claims.assertion: This was a rider-side cancellation of an on-demand RydeX trip, so the $6.61 cancellation fee can only stand if the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching; the record shows the fee of $6.61 was charged on a cancellation by the rider.

The rider cancelled 3 min 1 s after acceptance (09:00:10 → 09:03:11), i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so NS-4 on its own would not waive the fee — which is why I put the case on the driver-side conditions in NS-1 being unmet, not on the 3-minute rule.

Although the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, GPS shows the cumulative time the driver spent within 200 m of the pickup point before cancellation was only 30 seconds, far short of the >180 s (3:01) requirement of NS-1(iii).

The driver only entered the pickup radius at 09:02:40 and the rider cancelled 31 seconds later (and 11 seconds after the "I'm Here" tap), so no 3-minute wait at the pickup point could have elapsed before cancellation — NS-1(iii) fails on the timeline facts alone.

The driver's written claim of having waited "more than 6 minutes at the stand" is a post-hoc statement contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which show eligibility for the fee never matured; the system records must prevail.
Because NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.

There is no in-app chat in this case, so no rider message establishing the driver's arrival/waiting position can be relied on and the driver's verbal account is not recordable consent or proof — the contested fee rests entirely on the system records above.

weaknesses: Timing cuts against us on the rider-side rule: per F3 the cancellation came at 09:03:11, 3 min 1 s after acceptance at 09:00:10, so it falls outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window of NS-4 and I cannot rely on that clause to void the fee.

The driver did genuinely reach the pickup point — F1 shows a closest approach of 39 m at 09:03:00 and F5 shows a valid "I'm Here" tap 39 m from the pickup — so NS-1(i)/(ii) and the driver's diligence are largely made out; my case turns only on the 3-minute waiting requirement in NS-1(iii).

The complaint self-reports a 'counterfactual' cancellation time of 181 s after matching, which the other side can use to argue the rider was already past the grace period and that the fee was at least arguably earned; I rely on the rider's message being an unrecorded statement while F3 is the system record.

The comparison in F2 (30 s within 200 m) is a cumulative measure and the driver's own tap time (F5) plus arrival record (F4) can be read as showing an intent to wait; a judge could still see only a 31-second gap and find the driver substantially compliant, which is why the refund rests narrowly on the strict NS-1(iii) threshold.

The rider profile (F13: 3 disputes in 90 d, 0 upheld) shows a pattern of unsuccessful claims that the driver's side may use to attack credibility; it is not decisive and no flag is warranted against the driver on F14 (0 disputes).

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: This was a rider-side cancellation of an on-demand RydeX trip, so the $6.61 cancellation fee can only stand if the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching; the record shows the fee of $6.61 was charged on a cancellation by the rider.

The rider cancelled 3 min 1 s after acceptance (09:00:10 → 09:03:11), i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so NS-4 on its own would not waive the fee — which is why I put the case on the driver-side conditions in NS-1 being unmet, not on the 3-minute rule.

Although the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, GPS shows the cumulative time the driver spent within 200 m of the pickup point before cancellation was only 30 seconds, far short of the >180 s (3:01) requirement of NS-1(iii).

The driver only entered the pickup radius at 09:02:40 and the rider cancelled 31 seconds later (and 11 seconds after the "I'm Here" tap), so no 3-minute wait at the pickup point could have elapsed before cancellation — NS-1(iii) fails on the timeline facts alone.

The driver's written claim of having waited "more than 6 minutes at the stand" is a post-hoc statement contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which show eligibility for the fee never matured; the system records must prevail.
Because NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.

There is no in-app chat in this case, so no rider message establishing the driver's arrival/waiting position can be relied on and the driver's verbal account is not recordable consent or proof — the contested fee rests entirely on the system records above.

weaknesses: Timing cuts against us on the rider-side rule: per F3 the cancellation came at 09:03:11, 3 min 1 s after acceptance at 09:00:10, so it falls outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window of NS-4 and I cannot rely on that clause to void the fee.

The driver did genuinely reach the pickup point — F1 shows a closest approach of 39 m at 09:03:00 and F5 shows a valid "I'm Here" tap 39 m from the pickup — so NS-1(i)/(ii) and the driver's diligence are largely made out; my case turns only on the 3-minute waiting requirement in NS-1(iii).

The complaint self-reports a 'counterfactual' cancellation time of 181 s after matching, which the other side can use to argue the rider was already past the grace period and that the fee was at least arguably earned; I rely on the rider's message being an unrecorded statement while F3 is the system record.

The comparison in F2 (30 s within 200 m) is a cumulative measure and the driver's own tap time (F5) plus arrival record (F4) can be read as showing an intent to wait; a judge could still see only a 31-second gap and find the driver substantially compliant, which is why the refund rests narrowly on the strict NS-1(iii) threshold.

The rider profile (F13: 3 disputes in 90 d, 0 upheld) shows a pattern of unsuccessful claims that the driver's side may use to attack credibility; it is not decisive and no flag is warranted against the driver on F14 (0 disputes).

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 181 s after matching (09:00:10 → 09:03:11), which is past the 3-minute free-cancellation window of 3:00, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable on its face.

Because the rider — not the driver — cancelled, the case is governed by the rider-cancellation branch (NS-4), not by the driver no-show branch (NS-1/NS-2); a fee is chargeable for any rider cancellation made more than 3 minutes after matching.

The driver did in fact reach the pick-up point: GPS shows first entry within 200 m at 09:02:40 and a closest approach of 39 m at 09:03:00, both before the rider's cancellation at 09:03:11, so the rider's "he still charged me for cancelling" grievance is not caused by driver non-arrival.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pick-up point, i.e. inside the 200 m pick-up zone, and the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40 — consistent with the driver genuinely being on scene and the rider failing to board rather than the driver abandoning the job.

There is no in-app chat at all, so the rider's assertion that "I told the driver I was two minutes away" is unsupported by any rider message; the only statement on record is the driver's account of waiting and calling twice, and the rider's own claim of having communicated cannot create a free-cancellation right.

Ryde publishes no rule allowing a rider to cancel free of charge because the driver is late and there is no ETA field in this case, so any lateness-based excuse does not displace the fee; the rider's remedy is a manual RydeHELP appeal, which the platform may consider on discretion.

The driver has a 4.4-year account, 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 days and zero disputes upheld against him, which is inconsistent with the picture of a driver who abandons riders at the pick-up point and should weigh against any account flag.

The rider's own counterfactual — cancelled 181 s after matching — confirms the cancellation occurred after the 3-minute mark, so on the system timeline (which outranks statements) the $6.61 charge is supported and no refund is warranted.

weaknesses: F2 shows the driver was within 200 m of the pick-up for only 30 s cumulatively before the cancellation, and F5 shows only 10 s inside the zone after tapping "I'm Here"; although this case is a rider-side cancellation (NS-4) and not a driver no-show claim (NS-1), the rider can argue the driver's short presence (F5: wait only 10 s after the tap) shows he had barely settled at the stand, undermining F9's claim of having "waited more than 6 minutes".

F9 is the driver's own written statement only — and the system's records (F4: platform arrival 09:02:40, F5: "I'm Here" at 09:03:00) show he was not at the pick-up until roughly 2.5 minutes after acceptance, so the "6 minutes waiting" assertion is contradicted by the timeline and cannot be relied on (G11-style statement-vs-record conflict).

The rider's message that she was "two minutes away" (F8 shows no chat, so it may have been a phone call not on record) may sit alongside F3's 181 s timing; if the rider can show a system-recorded or in-app message of that kind, the fact pattern shifts toward a discretionary goodwill waiver under NS-7, which Ryde may grant despite the fee being valid.

points.response: Conceded on the timing half only: F3 does show cancellation at 09:03:11, 181 s after acceptance, so NS-4's 3-minute window is not available to us; that is precisely why our case is not built on NS-4 but on the fact that no driver-side cancellation/waiting charge can be validated here.

This misreads NS-0: NS-0 routes a rider-side cancellation to NS-4, but NS-4 addresses only whether a fee may be charged on cancellation timing — it does not cure the driver-side conditions of NS-1, and the fee on record (F6) is the same $6.61 the driver claims by treating this as a rider no-show.

We do not dispute that the driver arrived; F1 and F4 show arrival at 09:02:40 and a 39 m closest approach at 09:03:00, so the refund is not premised on non-arrival but on the fact that F2 records only 30 s within 200 m before cancellation, and F5 only 10 s of presence after the "I'm Here" tap.

The driver's arrival is genuine but incomplete: NS-1 requires both presence at the pickup (ii) and more than 3 minutes of waiting there (iii), and F5's 10 s and F2's 30 s fall short of the >180 s threshold, so the fee is not chargeable against the rider even where arrived.

Agreed there is no in-app chat (F8); but that cuts both ways — the driver's only evidence of the 6-minute wait is his own statement (F9), which the system records F4/F5 contradict, so the fee rests on an unsupported statement rather than the records.

We do not rely on a lateness-based free cancellation, so NS-7 is beside the point; the rider's complaint is not that the driver was late but that a $6.61 fee (F6) was charged without the driver-side conditions of NS-1 ever being met, which under NS-2 must be refunded.

We do not seek any account flag against the driver, and F14 is not contested; the driver's long history is irrelevant to the only issue, which is the strict NS-1(iii) waiting threshold measured in F2 and F5.

The 181 s timing (F3) is common ground but establishes only that the rider passed the grace period, not that the driver earned the fee; because F2 and F5 show the 3-minute pickup wait never developed, the charge fails on the NS-1 conditions and NS-2 requires refund_full.

Correct as far as it goes, and it defeats the rider's own case: NS-0 routes a rider-side cancellation of an on-demand RydeX trip through NS-4 only, and the fee of $6.61 was recorded on a rider cancellation (F3, F6), so no driver-side no-show clause can be invoked by the rider.

The rider expressly concedes the fee falls outside NS-4's 3-minute window (F3: accepted 09:00:10, cancelled 09:03:11), and NS-0 makes NS-4 the only route for a rider-side cancellation — so once NS-4 is satisfied the fee stands and NS-1/NS-2 are simply not the applicable branch.

NS-1(iii) is a condition for a driver claiming a rider no-show against a passive rider; here the rider cancelled the trip herself (F3), so the 3:01 waiting threshold of NS-1(iii) never becomes an element of the charge and its failure proves nothing about NS-4.

The timeline shows the driver still arrived at the pick-up and stayed inside the 200 m zone while the rider cancelled 31 s after arrival (F4, F5), and the only reason the pre-cancellation in-zone time is short is that the rider ended the trip 31 s later — the rider cannot manufacture a shortfall by cancelling early.

I do not rest on the driver's statement (F9): the system records alone establish arrival (F4: platform recorded arrival 09:02:40), in-zone proximity (F1: 39 m at 09:03:00) and a valid "I'm Here" tap (F5), which is all the driver-side diligence NS-4 requires before the rider is charged.

NS-2 applies only where a driver cancels on an alleged no-show and the NS-1 conditions fail; it cannot be used to refund a fee charged on the rider's own cancellation 3:01 after matching (F3), which NS-4 makes chargeable.

The rider is right that no in-app chat exists (F8), and that is exactly why the fee rests on the system records (F3, F4, F5) — but the rider's own unrecorded claim of being "two minutes away" is equally absent from those records and cannot displace them.
I withdraw nothing: D2's point stands on NS-0/NS-4, and the rider's brief itself concedes (C2) that the cancellation was past the 3-minute window.
